clue.text: Intense neurosis created by the weather

definitions.meaning: a severe, profound bout of low mood and despondency
meteorologists' term for a very low-pressure system bringing storms

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist blames a patient's severe anxiety on the gloomy weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses join an intensifier to the noun: a severe mental slump, and an intense area of low atmospheric pressure in forecasts.

clue.text: Cockney has to finish in time for eggs

indicators.note: the word for the finish is placed inside the word for the egg season

parts.note: Easter is the season of chocolate eggs
end means finish

explanation.surface: A Londoner must wrap things up by the springtime egg festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. A Cockney is a working-class Londoner, traditionally born in the East End of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cockney is traditionally a native of London's eastern districts, the area east of the City.

clue.text: Gun a man on board

definitions.meaning: slang for a handgun or firearm
a chessman or draughtsman on the playing board

explanation.surface: A gunman is aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang calls a firearm a 'piece', and each chessman moved on the board is likewise a playing token of that name.

clue.text: Choose baton and note for a conductor.

parts.note: to elect is to choose
a rod, as a baton is a short stick
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: An orchestra conductor picks up a baton and reads a note.
explanation.walkthrough: The orchestral 'baton', 'note' and 'conductor' all mislead: the conductor is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrode is a terminal that carries electric current into or out of a device, so it conducts electricity.

clue.text: A crude preliminary sketch that club swingers don't like to get into

definitions.meaning: a first draft drawing made before the finished version

definitions.text: that club swingers don't like to get into
definitions.meaning: golfers swinging clubs dislike landing in the long grass beside the fairway

explanation.surface: An artist's first sketch, describing a place golfers avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft drawing is a 'rough', and in golf the long grass bordering the fairway shares the same name.

clue.text: So if I crop this mixture it could be sleep-inducing

indicators.note: a mixture of these letters signals they are to be shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Cutting a crop into a herbal mixture might make a sleeping draught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this mixture' tells you to rearrange the letters of SO IF I CROP.
explanation.definitionFit: Something soporific induces drowsiness, like a sedative or a dull lecture.

clue.text: Unfit in start of exercises and physical training

indicators.note: the start of a word means its opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone out of shape at the start of a gym session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes E from 'exercises'.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means lacking skill or aptitude, so unsuitable or incompetent for a task.

clue.text: Having a certain disposition that could be good or bad

definitions.text: Having a certain disposition that could be good or bad

parts.words: Having a certain disposition that could be good or bad
parts.note: the word for having a temperament completes both good- and ill-tempered compounds, preceded by 'good' or 'ill'

explanation.surface: A description of someone's temperament, which might be pleasant or unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is mostly met attached to another: good-natured or ill-natured.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means possessing a particular temperament, usually prefixed to say what kind.

clue.text: Rise initially in. water vapour from rivulet

indicators.note: the first letter of the rise is placed inside the word for water vapour

parts.note: steam is water vapour

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Vapour rising first from a small brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes R from 'Rise'; 'in' puts it into STEAM. The stray full stop after 'in' is an OCR slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A rivulet is a small running watercourse, a brook or stream.

clue.text: One sense of direction in gallery

indicators.note: the compass direction is placed inside the name of the gallery

parts.note: the Tate is a famous London art gallery
S for south, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A visitor finds their bearings in an art gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of major British art galleries, the best known in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is one of the five senses, along with sight, hearing, smell and touch.

clue.text: Make fun of people in French, and tackle

indicators.note: the words for joking and for people go inside the French conjunction

parts.note: et is the French word for and
to quip is to make a witty jibe
men means people

explanation.surface: Mocking French people, and then tackling them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal; the setter uses the French conjunction for 'and' as the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Tackle is gear or apparatus, as in fishing tackle, which is kit for a task.

clue.text: Component part that cannot be resolved

definitions.meaning: a constituent or ingredient of a whole
in chemistry, a substance not resolvable into simpler substances

explanation.surface: A piece of something that cannot be broken down further.
explanation.definitionFit: An element is one constituent of a larger whole, and in chemistry a substance that cannot be split into simpler ones by chemical means.

clue.text: One who succeeds her with it alternatively

parts.note: or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Someone comes after a woman, or else after something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeeds' looks like 'comes after her', but it means inherits.
explanation.definitionFit: A heritor is an heir, one who inherits property and so succeeds to it.

clue.text: Two mothers, joining an another woman

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
dam is the mother of an animal, especially a horse

explanation.surface: Two mothers meet a third woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The two mothers are MA and DAM, joined together; the 'an' is an evident misprint in the printed clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a polite form of address for a lady, so it names a woman.

clue.text: Dr Hill's method in vehicular exhibition

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
tor is a rocky hill, with the 's giving S
how means the method or manner

explanation.surface: A doctor's technique demonstrated at a car exhibition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dr Hill' reads as a person, but splits into a doctor (MO) and a hill (TOR). A tor is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor show is a public exhibition displaying new cars and other vehicles.

clue.text: Beyond control immediately

definitions.meaning: unruly, as with children getting unmanageable
at once, without considering, as in dismissing something summarily

explanation.surface: Something gets unmanageable at once.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes things grown unmanageable, and also a refusal given at once without thought.

clue.text: Equipment needed to track a record — belonging to BR

definitions.text: Equipment needed to track a record
definitions.meaning: the rotating platter of a gramophone on which a disc plays
the rotating platform British Rail used to turn locomotives

explanation.surface: Gear for following a disc, owned by British Rail.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, the former UK national railway; 'track' plays on both the groove and the railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: A record deck's spinning platter and a railway's revolving platform for turning engines share the same name.

clue.text: Crafty trick right for a mechanic

parts.note: an artifice is a clever trick or stratagem

explanation.surface: A sly trick is just the thing for a mechanic.
explanation.definitionFit: An artificer is a skilled craftsman, especially a military or naval technician who repairs equipment.

clue.text: Original clothing the driver gets into

parts.note: first means original, earliest
gear means clothes

explanation.surface: A motorist pulls on the original outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets into' suggests dressing, but it is engaging a gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Lowest ratio of a car gearbox, the one a motorist engages to move off.

clue.text: Peevish as a jigsaw puzzle, may be?

definitions.meaning: irritable, inclined to worry
a jigsaw puzzle is cut with a fretsaw, so it is full of fretwork

explanation.surface: Someone grows irritable doing a jigsaw.
explanation.walkthrough: Jigsaw puzzles were cut with a fretsaw, so one is full of fretwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Peevish and anxious are synonyms of the word, which also reads as full of frets, the fretwork cuts of a jigsaw.

clue.text: Skin copper and sit back

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: back means the word for sitting is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A policeman takes off his skin and sits back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' is the reversal signal. 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but here it is the metal's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutis is the anatomical Latin term for the true skin or dermis.

clue.text: A short time for one in a corner

definitions.meaning: a brief moment, as in 'just a moment'
a boxer's attendant who stands in the fighter's corner

explanation.surface: Someone stands in a corner briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a brief instant and a boxer's helper, who waits in the corner between rounds.

clue.text: Quack known only by experience

definitions.meaning: an old word for a charlatan doctor relying on practice not science
based on observation rather than theory

explanation.surface: A fake doctor learnt everything through practice.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the word named a physician working from experience alone, hence a charlatan, and as an adjective means derived from observation.

clue.text: Part of Highland dress softly designed

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for softly
laid, as in plans laid, means designed or devised

explanation.surface: Scottish garments designed in a gentle style.
explanation.walkthrough: P (piano) is the musical marking for playing softly. Highland dress is traditional Scottish costume.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaid is the tartan cloth worn over the shoulder in Scottish costume.

clue.text: Church vessel to turn over persistently

parts.note: an urn is a vessel

explanation.surface: A church vase keeps being turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: To churn is to stir or agitate repeatedly, as in a butter churn or a churning mind.

clue.text: Trade in lots of vehicles

definitions.meaning: to deal in, especially illicit goods
the cars and lorries on the roads

explanation.surface: Dealing in many vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means illicit dealing, as in drug trafficking, and also the flow of vehicles on the roads.

clue.text: A collection of records from local bumpkin

indicators.note: from indicates the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A country yokel's record collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' draws the run out of 'local bumpkin'.
explanation.definitionFit: An album is a set of recordings issued together, or a book of collected items.

clue.text: Showy source of flowers used by photographers

parts.note: flash means ostentatious
a bulb grows into a flower

explanation.surface: A showy gardener's bulb, popular with photographers.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: something used by photographers.
explanation.definitionFit: Early cameras used a single-use glass lamp that gave a brilliant burst of light for exposure.

clue.text: Shakespeare's playwright? It could be rasher!

definitions.meaning: Francis ..., claimed by some to have written Shakespeare's plays
a rasher is a slice of cured pork; 'rasher' also means more reckless

explanation.surface: A theory that Shakespeare's plays had another author might be reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: The Baconian theory holds that Francis Bacon wrote Shakespeare's plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon is the supposed true author in one theory, and cured pork is sold in slices called rashers.

clue.text: Titled female of the lake-having only one supporter?

definitions.text: Titled female of the lake-having only one supporter?

parts.words: Titled female of the lake-having only one supporter?
parts.note: a lady named after an English lake, whose single fan alludes to the title of Oscar Wilde's play about her fan

explanation.surface: A noblewoman from the Lake District with just one admirer.
explanation.walkthrough: In Wilde's comedy the title character owns a fan; a fan is also a supporter. Windermere is the largest lake in England's Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Wilde's heroine bears a title and the name of an English lake, and her play is named after her fan.
